blocks.text: The ACSM 2026 overview of 137 systematic reviews found that muscle growth did not depend on details such as load or how often you train, once weekly sets were equal. Its main advice: hard sets, at least twice a week, for all major muscles.

title: Easy, moderate and hard cardio

blocks.text: Cardio guidelines count minutes of moderate or vigorous activity. You can judge both without a heart-rate monitor by rating your effort from 0 to 10, relative to your own fitness.

blocks.title: Effort out of 10, relative to your fitness

items.label: Light
items.text: Everyday movement such as slow walking.

items.label: Moderate
items.text: Counts toward 150 to 300 minutes a week.

items.label: Vigorous
items.text: Counts toward 75 to 150 minutes a week.

blocks.title: Three ways to meet the weekly minimum

items.title: Moderate
items.text: Brisk walk, 30 minutes on Monday, Wednesday and Friday: 90 moderate minutes.

items.title: Vigorous
items.text: Jog, 15 minutes on Tuesday and Saturday: 30 vigorous minutes.

items.title: Add up
items.text: One vigorous minute counts as two moderate ones, so 90 + 2 x 30 = 150. The minimum is met.

blocks.text: WHO rates light activity at 2 to 4, moderate at 5 or 6 and vigorous at 7 or 8 on a 0 to 10 scale of perceived exertion, relative to each person's capacity.
Running uses a talk test for the same idea; see the Running chapter. Lifting uses a different scale, reps in reserve, in the next chapter.

blocks.title: Key points
items: Rate cardio effort 0 to 10: 5 or 6 is moderate, 7 or 8 is vigorous.
One vigorous minute counts like two moderate minutes toward the weekly target.
Mix both to reach at least 150 moderate-equivalent minutes a week.

blocks.text: Good technique means repeating the same movement, under control, through a range you own. Learn each lift light, and add weight only when every rep looks and feels the same.

blocks.title: Learning a new lift: Levlofit rules

items.title: Start light
items.text: Bodyweight, a light dumbbell or an empty bar.

items.title: Same setup
items.text: Place your feet, hands and grip the same way on every rep.

items.title: Control the way down
items.text: Lower the weight under control instead of dropping into the bottom.

items.title: Use the range you own
items.text: Go as deep as you can while keeping your position, without pain.

items.title: Check it
items.text: Film one set from the side and compare it with the exercise demo.

items.title: Then add weight
items.text: Only when every rep looks the same, keeping 2 to 3 reps in reserve while you learn.

do.title: Ready for more weight
items: Every rep has the same speed and shape
You finish the set with reps in reserve
No pain in any joint, during or the next day

dont.title: Fix before adding weight
items: Reps change shape or speed as the set goes on
You reach failure earlier than planned
Joint pain during or after the lift; see Soreness, pain and injuries

blocks.text: Dynamic stretching has no negative effect and can help performance. Long static stretches cause a small, short-lived drop in force, so keep them after training.
